per_shot.note: The serpent is only a cropped dark-red faceted chunk at the top-left edge. It has no glow and casts no light, and the frame is really about the lava pool and the beam. The green mote swirl near it reads as a different creature.
The Long One isn't in the close-up at all. It's the pod on veined rock, so the close-up fails at its one job.
No creature reads. The only candidate is a dull grey-olive tile beside the pod, which looks like an unlit block rather than an ore that bites. It has no mouth, no teeth and no glow.
The grey tile is larger here but still a flat, dead square with no geode faceting, no ore glow and no tell. Nothing says threat.

Two black capsules ringed by orange spark particles. They're readable as figures against the warm core chamber, but a pursuer made of light is drawn as two black voids. They cast no light on the floor, and the core-chamber glow out-competes them.

Up close they're still opaque black pills with sparkle noise. There's no body, no face and no bright core, and no light lands on the stone at their feet. The silhouette is legible but reads as a placeholder.
Slate-blue triangular shards scattered in the beam read as ice debris, not winged creatures. They're unlit and not emissive, so the CRYOS hue is right but they're invisible outside the lamp.
The shards are pushed to the top-right corner, partly cut off and dim. The wing shape is barely suggested, nothing glows and nothing threatens.

top_issues.issue: Creatures are missing from or cropped out of their own showcase frames
top_issues.why: A sandbox shot that doesn't show the creature can't be judged and reads as broken. The close-ups especially just frame the pod.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Frame each capture on the creature, with the pod as a scale reference, and make sure the whole body is in frame and unoccluded. The close-up should centre the creature, not the pod.

top_issues.issue: No self-light: none of the four creatures glow or light the rock around them
top_issues.why: This breaks the house rule 'glow that lands'. The Warden, Shellbacks and Glimmerflies all bloom and wash their surroundings, while these are dark, matte and only visible when the headlamp hits them.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each creature emissive parts in its world hue plus a small point light that pools on nearby blocks. Long One: amber-ember seams along its segments. Mimic: an ore glow that flares at the bite. Rimewings: ice-cyan wing edges. Kindled: a bright core, see below.

top_issues.issue: The Kindled, a pursuer made of light, is drawn as black capsules
top_issues.why: It inverts the creature's identity. Black pills with spark noise read as a placeholder or a void-shadow, not a being of light. It's also visually weaker than the core chamber it stands in.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Invert the value: a bright, near-white-hot faceted figure with a warm halo and a hard light cast on the floor ahead of it. Keep a low-poly silhouette (head, shoulders, lean toward the player) so it reads as a pursuer. If the darkness is intentional, it needs a burning rim or core so it still reads as light.

top_issues.issue: The Geode Mimic doesn't read as a creature or a threat
top_issues.why: A flat grey tile is the least readable thing in a frame full of glowing veins. The player can't tell it apart from dead rock, and nothing marks the dangerous end.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Make it a convincing ore block with a deliberate tell (a slightly wrong glow colour, a hairline seam, faint breathing). When it opens, show a faceted geode-crystal maw with a glowing interior that lights the surrounding blocks. Show the open or tell state in the sandbox shot.

top_issues.issue: Rimewings read as floating debris shards, not winged creatures
top_issues.why: Loose dark triangles have no body, no wing pairs and no head, so at play size they look like particles. They're only visible inside the beam.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Build each rimewing as a small chunky body with two angled faceted wing plates, ice-cyan emissive edges and a faint cold glow that tints the dark blue rock. Flock them in a readable formation, closer to the pod and fully in frame.

protect: The habitat lighting: the VEIL lava pools, amber beam, glowing fissures and dust in the lamp beam read strongly as VEIL-3
The CRYOS habitat palette: the cold blue rock and white-blue beam clearly read as the ice world
The core-chamber staging behind the Kindled: warm flood light, pillars, floating core shards
The pod design: chunky faceted white body, glowing teal visor, orange trim
The Rimewings' faceted low-poly shard language and blue hue, as a starting point for the wings
The Kindled's orange spark particles, as an accent around a bright body
